response.sql: SELECT language_id, AVG(replacement_cost) AS avg_replacement_cost, AVG(length) AS avg_running_time FROM film WHERE length >= 112 GROUP BY language_id ORDER BY avg_running_time IS NULL, avg_running_time DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: A film is 'long' when length is greater than or equal to 112 minutes (the cutoff is inclusive).
'Language' means film.language_id, not original_language_id, as the request specifies.

AVG skips NULLs, so each average ignores missing values. Both averaged columns are NOT NULL in this schema, and the WHERE clause excludes NULL lengths, so no average can be NULL and the NULLS-LAST ordering is a safeguard only (MySQL syntax via IS NULL).

alternatives.interpretation: 'Long' means strictly longer than 112 minutes, so a film of exactly 112 minutes is excluded.
